reasonDefinitions.changed-ordered-validation: The mixed predicate was replaced by ordered, domain-named validation phases while preserving the original first failure, bounds, identity binding, and independent evidence checks.
reasonDefinitions.changed-readiness-proof: Snapshot acquisition is now separate from named release, role, forbidden-grant, and capability assertions; the same single transaction, SQL order, and fail-closed result remain.
reasonDefinitions.changed-consistency-phases: The orchestration now names its typed admission, identity, control-state, or completion-policy phases while retaining one transaction/snapshot and the original query and mutation order.
reasonDefinitions.changed-workflow-proof: The coupled workflow proof now exposes join identity, invocation scope, iteration, and loop topology phases while retaining cached traversal, compatibility allowances, bounds, and first failure.
reasonDefinitions.changed-owned-lifetime: Resource acquisition, operation, and ordered cleanup are now expressed through owner-local phases with original/cleanup error identity, all-attempted behavior, cancellation, and idempotence preserved.
reasonDefinitions.changed-provider-lifetime: Provider-specific admission and outcome policy remain local while credential/body ownership is bounded by an explicit phase that always zeroizes or closes the owned resource.
reasonDefinitions.changed-moved-q9-owner: The snapshot locator moved during the preceding Q9 correction; its replacement explicitly owns stream/body cleanup and preserves synchronous throws, rejected writes, bounds, and original error precedence.
reasonDefinitions.retained-test-suite: This is a describe/test callback that groups independently named scenarios; setup and oracle values remain visible in each case, and extracting the container would add navigation without reducing behavioral reasoning.
reasonDefinitions.retained-test-fixture: This test helper is the local deterministic fixture/emulator owner used by named scenarios; its explicit state and failure injection are part of the test oracle and a generic helper would hide them.
reasonDefinitions.retained-declarative-composition: This function is a declarative module, registry, metrics, or capability composition root whose length comes from explicit field-to-owner wiring; splitting it would scatter the dependency map without simplifying control flow.
reasonDefinitions.retained-transaction-proof: The function keeps one transaction, lock/lease, query order, and atomic mutation proof visible. Further extraction would pass most of the transaction state through helpers and obscure failure or consistency ordering.
reasonDefinitions.retained-bounded-parser: The explicit branches form a bounded parser/traversal with contract-specific diagnostics and first-failure order; a data-driven or shared validator would obscure limits, compatibility, or cached traversal state.
reasonDefinitions.retained-state-machine: The branches are the local domain state machine and share evolving checkpoint/lease/coordinator state; extraction would fragment transition precedence or require a callback-heavy descriptor.
reasonDefinitions.retained-resource-owner: This is the existing resource owner: acquisition state, primary failure, all required cleanup attempts, and combined-failure ordering are intentionally visible together; a shared lifecycle framework would add indirection.
reasonDefinitions.retained-security-boundary: The compound check is one fail-closed cross-field security/identity admission invariant with a single public error contract; splitting it would not remove mental execution and could alter validation precedence.
reasonDefinitions.retained-independent-policy: The condition is a domain-local compatibility, integrity, or policy rule with distinct bounds and diagnostics; equal-looking literals or checks elsewhere do not share its authority.
reasonDefinitions.retained-benchmark-summary-agreement: The short predicate compares every named statistic with an independently recomputed summary; keeping the metric iteration beside the single mismatch error makes the oracle more explicit than a one-use wrapper.
reasonDefinitions.retained-benchmark-measurement-shape: The homogeneous guard admits one bounded SQL or sampled-observation record before later calculations. Its fields, numeric bounds, and one public diagnostic are clearer together than split across one-use predicates.
reasonDefinitions.retained-benchmark-observation-sample: The local sample guard applies the same finite, non-negative rule to the four explicitly named database metrics after validating the timestamp; extracting its callback would hide the measured fields without reducing branching.
reasonDefinitions.retained-scenario-identity: The predicate is the single scenario-name identity proof: map cardinality detects duplicates while the adjacent callback rejects missing names. A helper would separate the two halves of the same index invariant.
reasonDefinitions.retained-compatibility-target-identity: The predicate proves that the exact epoch, fingerprint, and canonical catalog target belongs to the already parsed supported set before any database query. Keeping all three identity fields together preserves the fail-closed preactivation boundary.
reasonDefinitions.retained-small-wrapper: The flagged size comes from a cohesive public facade over private operations or explicit result mapping; the wrapper has no mixed lifetime or policy decision that a further split would clarify.

newFindings.reason: Production heartbeat start, durable-abort/failure observation, execution cancellation, and joined stop now have one visible owner.
Preview deadline and lease-loss races remain preview-specific but their timer, heartbeat, execution signal, and joined stop are now one phase.
Artifact ownership now reads as bounded spool, pending record, upload verification, finalize, and directory cleanup without extra copies.
Only repeated timing, recovery logging, failure backoff, cancellation, and polling delay are shared; all eight operation meanings remain in named loops.
Claim observation, publication, settlement, failed-publication release, and batch aggregation are now named local phases with original capacity scheduling and settlement order.
Retry versus terminal policy is a discriminated decision tested across side-effect, dispatch, prior uncertainty, and exhaustion combinations before the original atomic SQL mutation.
Definition and executor successor rules are separate typed phases preserving authoritative transitions and first failure.
Two opaque inline subprocess programs became readable separate-process fixtures while preserving barriers, timing provenance, environment identity, and failure behavior.
A named context replaces paired dispatch-state booleans at abort and signal-race boundaries, preserving every possibly-dispatched and ambiguity combination.
The remaining mixed predicate is one fail-closed prepared-node identity and scope admission rule; splitting it would not reduce the coupled proof and could change failure precedence.
The extracted owner isolates operation population and contract-shape admission from later sample and evidence traversal while preserving short-circuit order.
Three explicit operation-evidence rules now remain together under the round-operation owner, after shape and population admission and before sample comparison.
Participant-set identity and non-empty overlap are now a named proof separate from environment and timing evidence.
Runtime, CPU, and database environment identity checks now have one ordered owner after evidence shape admission.
Named-test interval containment is separated from result production and retains the original first invalid suite.
Producer, result, and source identity binding now precedes interval traversal and hashing in the original failure order.
This is the bounded compatibility refinement for legacy empty scopes and V2 invocation identities; a generic predicate would obscure version-specific allowances.
The condition is the single fact projection rule that distinguishes completed inline output from all other physical observations inside one repeatable-read proof.
Forbidden direct grants are now a named readiness assertion over the one acquired privilege snapshot.
Required and forbidden operator capabilities are now checked by a named assertion without converting the explicit privilege inventory into a permissive generic loop.
The additional branch condition is part of the existing cached bounded reconvergence traversal and keeps its distinct graph diagnostic and first-failure order.
The compound rule is one structured-scope boundary tying collection identity, item index, and invocation scope; extraction would fragment that admission proof.
Invocation node, ancestor, branch-port, and key membership are now an ordered named phase that reuses the already parsed executable graph.
Loop identity and topology compatibility are now a named phase preserving V1/V2 allowances, bounds, and the original error precedence.
This is baseline C127 reconciled from its callback locator to the inferred constructor owner; its expression-engine admission rule and error contract are unchanged.
The new long test callback is the describe container for an explicit completion-policy matrix; cases keep inputs, mutations, and oracles visible rather than hiding them in production-derived helpers.
Baseline C093 moved to the request-admission module; its ordered name, blocked-header, value, duplicate, count, and byte rules are preserved under one parser owner.
Baseline C094 moved to the request-admission module and retains independent count and value-length policies before deduplication and longest-first ordering.

The final duplication pass found one genuinely identical production/preview projection; only optional provider-dispatch and capability fields are shared, while supervision and dispatch policy remain separate.
Pending failure rows now validate and append directly to the owning observation sequence, preserving database order without an intermediate batch and spread.
Three identical inline/artifact/absent output comparisons now share one discriminated domain predicate; wait-state logic with intentionally different absent-output semantics remains local.
Request-mode input selection and persisted preview output projection are now two named mappings instead of nested conditional object construction.
The waiting-success, waiting-failure, and terminal fact requirements now read as an ordered domain mapping while retaining the original reverse-scan and first inconsistency.
Legacy retention outcome derivation now states completed, stale, and progressed precedence explicitly rather than nesting validation and cursor predicates.
Persisted join validation now names required arrivals, satisfiability, and expected failure reason while preserving all/any/count semantics and diagnostic order.
Loop parent validation now exposes terminal, cancellation, deadline, complete, and active-state precedence without a nested conditional expression.
Client release now derives rollback, cancellation, absent-error, and non-Error rollback outcomes in one ordered cleanup policy.
Readiness, delete, purge, and verification use one identical two-region failure attribution policy instead of four nested conditional copies.
Provider rate-limit, unavailable, and rejection precedence is now explicit before construction of the normalized connection-test outcome.
Generated, existing, and absent webhook endpoint-key selection now has one named precedence rule instead of nested hashing branches.
Lifecycle conflict, revision conflict, and base problem response construction now has an explicit ordered mapper with its base contract type visible.
